conviction_note: Lean negative but moderated: the Q4 bar sits at the top of the company's implied Q4 EPS range ($0.53-0.57; Street $0.56-0.57) and needs comps to accelerate from 1.2% to roughly 2.7-4.7%, revenue consensus ($352-360M, two disagreeing sources) implies +4.8-7% growth against Q3's +1.8% and a revenue miss in Q3, Sprouts (same July-September months, same natural/organic channel) printed traffic -3.3% and a September visit dip and announced a January 2027 price reset, and the Street's FY27 EPS of $2.32 (+10%) is above what this company's conservative initial guides have looked like; against that the stock is -18.6% in 20 days, -9.7% in 5 and -5% intraday on the print day with no news, and short interest was 7.7% of float at ~8 days to cover, so p_up sits at 43 rather than the mid-30s; findings sum -2.4 against a scaled -1.12, the gap being that the scaled number carries the squeeze/low-bar uncertainty in p_up while the findings are each sized on their own.

findings.finding: The stock went into the print at $26.36, -18.6% over 20 sessions, -9.7% over 5 and -5.2% intraday on the print day, ~38% below the $42.25 mean target, with no analyst rating change in the prior month and no company news found for the last week; the bar the market actually holds is therefore below the Street's top-of-range $0.56-0.57 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two positive reactions in the baseline (+30.24% May 2025, +6.7% Aug 2025) came off lower bases; the last four prints were all negative (-12.54, -4.86, -2.22, -5.04).
findings.why_not_priced: This IS the price; the point is that consensus EPS was not revised down with it (Street FY26 still $2.11 at the top of the range on 2026-11-11), so a print at consensus clears a lower real bar. If the drawdown had been driven by a known estimate cut, the estimates would have moved; they have not.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers notes sentiment turned more bearish into the print (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NGVC/23183). The last-5-day fall itself is unexplained, which caps this finding small.

findings.finding: Q4 EPS consensus of $0.56 (Chartmill) / $0.57 (Benzinga) sits at the top of the company's implied Q4 range of $0.53-0.57 (FY26 guide $2.07-2.11 less 9M EPS $1.54), and reaching it requires Q4 daily-average comps of roughly 2.7-4.7% (FY 1.5-2.0% after a 1.1% nine-month comp) against Q3's 1.2% and a +4.2% year-ago compare, plus gross margin recovering from 29.3% to near the year-ago 29.5% without the $2.0M insurance gain that helped Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EPS missed $0.52 by $0.04 with GM -60bp and the stock fell 12.54%; Q4 FY25 EPS $0.51 with GM -10bp and an initial guide, -5.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved off the top of the range (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11: Street FY26 $2.11 'the very top of the revised range'); if the market had priced a miss, the estimate would sit at the midpoint ($0.55) or below. Partly priced by the 19% slide.
findings.independence: The two-year stack argues the other way: Q3 two-year comp 8.6%, and holding 8.6% on a 4.2% compare implies ~4.4% Q4 comps; management said Q3 comps improved sequentially through the quarter and called the margin pressure 'isolated to this quarter' (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/NGVC/Q32026). Shares the comp-acceleration premise with the revenue finding below; sized net of that overlap.

findings.finding: Q4 revenue consensus of $352.1M (Benzinga) to $359.65M (Chartmill) implies +4.8% to +7.0% growth on $336.1M, against Q3's +1.8% growth, Q3's $12.5M (3.6%) revenue miss, and one fewer Q4 selling day (stores closed Labor Day) flagged on the Q3 call; comps ~3% plus H2 store openings point nearer $349-352M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 revenue missed $347.2M by 3.6% and the stock fell 12.54% (revenue miss and EPS miss together).
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue estimates (snippets of https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NGVC/earnings-forecasts and https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/NGVC/estimates) still embed growth 3-4x Q3's; if the Street had absorbed the Q3 miss and the selling-day loss the figure would be ~$345-350M. Bar is two disagreeing sources, so capped small.
findings.independence: Year-ago base and Q3 growth from company releases (https://finviz.com/news/235464/natural-grocers-by-vitamin-cottage-announces-fiscal-2025-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results; SEC Q3 exhibit). Store openings in H2 (Walla Walla May 20, Appleton Sept 30, two after Q3 end) add some growth (https://finviz.com/news/392538/natural-grocers-opens-its-doors-in-appleton-wisconsin-with-a-grand-opening-celebration-on-september-30-2026). Shares the comp premise with the EPS finding.

findings.finding: Sprouts, the closest listed natural/organic peer, reported its July-September quarter (the same calendar months as NGVC's Q4) on 2026-10-28 with comps -0.9%, comparable transactions -3.3% ('units, traffic, and frequency are not recovering, even against easier compares'), Placer.ai same-store visits roughly flat for the quarter with a September dip, and a Q4 comp guide of -2% to -4%.
findings.link: Same channel and customer (natural/organic specialty grocery, health-focused shopper), overlapping states (CO, TX, AZ and others), identical calendar months (SFM Q3 = Jul-Sep = NGVC fiscal Q4); NGVC's own Q3 transactions were already -1.8%. No shared-revenue figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NGVC's Q3 print (transactions -1.8%, comps +1.2%) fell 12.54%; traffic has been the named watch item in the preview.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: NGVC's 20-day slide largely followed the SFM print. But NGVC's own Q4 consensus did not come down to match (still top of range), so the read-through has reached the price more than the estimates.
findings.independence: Placer.ai: Sprouts same-store visits -0.1% for Q3 with a September dip (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/sprouts-finds-steadier-ground-in-q3-2026, 2026-10-21); StockStory call recap (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/sfm/news/earnings-call/sfm-q3-deep-dive-pricing-reset-and-affordability-investments-prompt-cautious-outlook). NGVC management says it does not see down-trading and is the price leader against its closest competitors (Q3 call), which cuts against transmission; sized as a proxy.

findings.finding: The FY27 initial guide is the line most likely to decide the reaction: the Street sits at FY27 EPS $2.32 (+10% on FY26's $2.07-2.11) and revenue $1.44B, while NGVC's last initial guide (FY26: EPS $2.00-2.15, comps 1.5-4.0%) was wide and ended flat, Sprouts launches a nationwide price reset on core and private-label items in January 2027 and reconsiders its pace, and NGVC's unit growth (4-5% a year) carries rising pre-opening costs ($0.08 a share in FY26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Initial FY26 guide on 2025-11-20: -5.04%; FY guide narrowed down on 2026-08-06: -12.54%; FY guide refined for consumer headwinds on 2026-05-07: -4.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street FY27 number has not been cut despite FY26 landing flat and the SFM price reset (no rating changes in the month to 2026-11-18 per AAII); if the market expected a sub-$2.30 midpoint, FY27 estimates would already be near $2.20-2.25.
findings.independence: Initial FY26 outlook table (https://finviz.com/news/235464/natural-grocers-by-vitamin-cottage-announces-fiscal-2025-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results); Sprouts price reset (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/sfm/news/earnings-call/sfm-q3-deep-dive-pricing-reset-and-affordability-investments-prompt-cautious-outlook); unit-growth and pre-opening commentary (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/NGVC/Q32026). All inference about a guide nobody has seen; shrunk for the crowded short.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call (2026-08-06) management said Q3 comps improved sequentially through the quarter, attributed part of the shrink to temporary effects of an ERP upgrade completed the prior quarter, and said the gross-margin pressure should be 'isolated to this quarter'; the year-ago Q4 gross margin to recover toward is 29.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin was the swing line on the last print (-60bp, -12.54%).
findings.why_not_priced: Stated on a call 15 weeks ago and partly reflected in the post-Q3 bounce to $29.15; the 19% slide since suggests the market no longer credits it. A margin print back at ~29.5% would be the 'one-off' confirmation the preview names as the validation point.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview names margin recovery toward 29.5% as the validation (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NGVC/23183). Same speaker for every piece; no independent margin series.

findings.finding: UNFI, NGVC's primary distributor (the one whose 2025 cyber incident hit NGVC's comparability), reported natural-segment sales +6.6% to $4.3B for its quarter to early August 2026, saying demand for natural, organic and specialty products remained strong and natural outpaced the broader market.
findings.link: UNFI is the distributor named in NGVC's releases (cyber-incident disclosure); its natural segment serves independent and specialty natural retailers including NGVC; overlap with NGVC's Q4 is only the May-early August months, and it includes new-customer onboarding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of NGVC reacting to UNFI prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A distributor's channel growth is not a series NGVC's holders track; but it only partly overlaps the quarter and includes share gains, so small.
findings.independence: Cuts against the Sprouts read-through; none other found.

findings.why_not_priced: Known since September and governance-only; the only connection to the window is that it became effective in the same week as the unexplained 9.7% slide. Nearly zero.

baseline_tension: No option skew to agree or disagree with; the negative lean agrees with the 18.6% 20-day slide and the name's habit of falling on prints, which means part of it is in the price, and the rising, ~8-day short is the main reason p_up is held at 43 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar from two disagreeing sources): revenue consensus is $352.1M vs $359.65M, so the revenue finding was capped from -1.5 to -1.0.

Rule 5 (an unexplained microcap drawdown is worth ~0): the expectations finding rests partly on a 5-day/intraday fall with no cause found, so it went from +1.5 to +0.8; the 20-day part is explained by the Sprouts print and kept.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): 7.67% of float at ~8 days to cover; the FY27-guide finding went from -2.0 to -1.7 and p_up moved from 42 to 43.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller than company data): the Sprouts read-through went from -1.0 to -0.8, with NGVC's own 'no down-trading' statement noted in independence.
Rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9 left the set standing: no financing, no segment, no one-off sized as operating profit (the Q3 insurance gain is only context in the EPS bar).
